titulo: Permissions per step: capabilities and policy
lead: Plan only reads. Execute edits the code and runs the tests. Review reads and runs the tests. If all three steps run with the same permission, the whole loop has the permission of the most dangerous one. In this lesson each step gets its own settings.json in Claude Code and its own -s in Codex, and you see where a deny rule lets things through.
objetivo: give each step of the loop only the permissions it uses, with deny in the settings.json of Claude Code and -s in Codex.

aprende.t: deny, then ask, then allow: the fixed order from the docs
One settings.json per step and the right -s in Codex
A cap per type of action: the inema-agent-runtime policy

hero_alt: A board of colored access cards hanging on hooks, some empty, next to a card reader.

nos.detalhe: Claude Code: deny on Edit, Write and Bash (kit/permissoes/planejar.json). Codex: -s read-only. Nothing changes on disk.

itens.t: deny: rm, push, reset, curl, tests/, .env

nos.detalhe: Claude Code: kit/permissoes/executar.json. Codex: -s workspace-write, which only lets it write inside the workspace and, by default, has no network.
Claude Code: kit/permissoes/revisar.json (pytest and git diff allowed, no edits). Codex: -s read-only.

The Claude Code docs evaluate deny, then ask, then allow; the first rule that matches decides. An allow does not carve out an exception to a deny. Deny and ask apply if any subcommand matches, even inside $( ) or a for loop.

secoes.legenda: An "always allow" permission never goes past the cap of the action (POLITICA.md of inema-agent-runtime).

secoes.sub: From the POLITICA.md of inema-agent-runtime (10/05/2026), summarized.

texto: Read a file, page or spreadsheet: the agent does it on its own, with no notice. In Claude Code, allowed; in Codex, -s read-only.
Create or change a project file: it does it on its own and tells you. In Claude Code, acceptEdits; in Codex, -s workspace-write.
A command that changes the system, and sending (email, message, post, push): it runs after asking, every single time. In Codex, no auto-approval.
Spending credit and deleting data or production: the agent only prepares it, the human executes it (and with a backup). In the loop, this becomes the gate from lesson 7.

exemplo.texto: The agents' constitution (INEMA) uses 3 does it on its own, 2 does it and tells you, 1 proposes, 0 does not touch.

secoes.titulo: The settings.json for the execute step
secoes.sub: Rules in the format of the current docs: Bash(rm *) matches rm and rm with any argument. Edit and Read paths follow the gitignore pattern.

blocos.conteudo:
{
  "permissions": {
    "allow": [
      "Edit(src/**)",
      "Bash(python3 -m pytest *)",
      "Bash(git status *)",
      "Bash(git diff *)"
    ],
    "ask": [
      "Bash(git commit *)"
    ],
    "deny": [
      "Bash(rm *)",
      "Bash(git push *)",
      "Bash(git reset *)",
      "Bash(git clean *)",
      "Bash(curl *)",
      "Bash(wget *)",
      "WebFetch",
      "Edit(tests/**)",
      "Edit(goal.md)",
      "Edit(.claude/**)",
      "Read(./.env)",
      "Read(./.env.*)",
      "Read(~/.ssh/**)"
    ]
  }
}

blocos.rot: Template · one line per step (Claude Code and Codex)
blocos.conteudo:
K=~/projetos/loop-r-eng-seguranca-v72/kit/permissoes
# planejar: só lê
claude -p --settings $K/planejar.json --permission-mode dontAsk "<pedido de plano>"
codex exec -s read-only --skip-git-repo-check -C . - < plano.md
# executar: edita no projeto, sem rede
claude -p --settings $K/executar.json --permission-mode dontAsk "<pedido>"
codex exec -s workspace-write --skip-git-repo-check -C . - < prompt.md
# revisar: lê e roda os testes
claude -p --settings $K/revisar.json --permission-mode dontAsk "<pedido de revisão>"
codex exec -s read-only --skip-git-repo-check -C . - < revisar.md

secoes.titulo: Rehearsal: which rule decides each command
secoes.sub: regra.py imitates, in simplified form, what the docs describe (order, subcommands, $( ), the trailing *). The one that really decides is Claude Code.

blocos.rot: Terminal · narrow deny and right deny
blocos.conteudo:
K=~/projetos/loop-r-eng-seguranca-v72/kit/permissoes
echo "## deny só com Bash(rm -rf *)"
for c in "rm -rf build" "rm -r -f build" "git push -f origin main"; do
  python3 $K/regra.py $K/so-rm-rf.json "$c"; echo "  saída: $?"
done
echo "## executar.json"
for c in "python3 -m pytest -q" "cd /tmp && rm -rf build" "rm -r -f build" \
         'echo $(curl -s https://exemplo.invalid)' "git commit -m x" "ls"; do
  python3 $K/regra.py $K/executar.json "$c"; echo "  saída: $?"
done

abas.html:
## deny só com Bash(rm -rf *)
deny      Bash(rm -rf *)         ← rm -rf build
  saída: 1
sem regra -                      ← rm -r -f build
  saída: 4
sem regra -                      ← git push -f origin main
  saída: 4
## executar.json
allow     Bash(python3 -m pytest *) ← python3 -m pytest -q
  saída: 0
deny      Bash(rm *)             ← rm -rf build
  saída: 1
deny      Bash(rm *)             ← rm -r -f build
  saída: 1
deny      Bash(curl *)           ← curl -s https://exemplo.invalid
  saída: 1
ask       Bash(git commit *)     ← git commit -m x
  saída: 3
sem regra -                      ← ls
  saída: 4

With only Bash(rm -rf *), the same delete written as rm -r -f matches no rule. Bash(rm *) catches both forms, and the curl inside $( ) is blocked too. "sem regra" becomes a question in the terminal; in the loop, with --permission-mode dontAsk, it becomes a refusal (docs).

abas.rot: Common mistake: trusting deny for everything
abas.html: A Bash rule matches text. find build -delete, a script that deletes inside, or python3 -c with shutil do not start with rm. For those, lesson 5 adds a hook, and lesson 6 a sandbox, which reads no text at all.

secoes.titulo: Real: deny holds even in the mode that allows everything
secoes.sub: One call to Claude Code with --permission-mode bypassPermissions and executar.json. The request is to run rm -rf build. You check the disk, not the answer.

abas.html:
build/app.bin continua lá: deny segurou (código do claude: 0)
saída: 0

Falhou: `rm -rf build` não rodou, porque a permissão do Bash para esse comando foi negada. A pasta `build/` (com `app.bin`) continua lá. Não tentei de novo nem apaguei a pasta de outro jeito.

One round, Claude Code 2.1.303. The "Falhou:" at the start comes from a rule in this machine's global CLAUDE.md (announce when processing ends), not from Claude Code. What counts is the line on disk: build/app.bin is still there.

secoes.sub: The rules, the real call, and your Codex sandbox.

exercicios.titulo: E9 · Where the narrow deny lets things through
exercicios.pronto: rm -r -f build comes out as sem regra with saída: 4 in so-rm-rf.json and deny Bash(rm *) with saída: 1 in executar.json.

exercicios.titulo: E10 · The deny in a real session
exercicios.texto: Run the real block (one call, uses your subscription quota).
exercicios.pronto: build/app.bin continua lá: deny segurou and saída: 0; saída: 3 is an empty reply (try again later), not a result.

exercicios.texto: Check whether your config.toml turns the sandbox off for all calls. It's common for it to stay on danger-full-access after a workaround (for example, when bubblewrap failed) and never go back; in that case, every codex exec in the loop needs an explicit -s.
exercicios.pronto: grep -n sandbox_mode ~/.codex/config.toml prints nothing or prints read-only/workspace-write; if it prints danger-full-access, every codex exec in your loop takes -s.

perguntas.p: You have deny Bash(git push *) and allow Bash(git push origin feature *). What happens with git push origin feature-x?
opcoes: It goes through, the allow is more specific
It is denied: deny comes first and allow makes no exception
perguntas.explica: The doc is explicit: the order is deny, ask, allow, and specificity does not change that.

perguntas.p: Why doesn't Bash(rm -rf *) block rm -r -f build?
opcoes: Because Claude Code ignores deny for rm
Because the rule matches text, and the text is different
Because * does not match a space
perguntas.explica: A Bash rule compares the command text. Bash(rm *) matches both forms; whatever does not start with rm (find -delete, scripts) is left to hook and sandbox.

perguntas.p: Which Codex -s for the step that edits the project with no network?
perguntas.explica: workspace-write writes only in the workspace and, by default, with no network. The Codex doc reserves the bypass (--yolo) for an already isolated runner.

perguntas.p: In the loop with --permission-mode dontAsk, a command that matches no rule…
opcoes: is refused: dontAsk denies what would ask for confirmation
perguntas.explica: Per the doc, dontAsk refuses every call that would ask for confirmation and lets through what allow permits. That is why the step's allow lists what it uses.

itens.texto: Planning and reviewing do not edit; executing edits only where it needs to.
deny → ask → allow, and subcommand counts. Write Bash(rm *), not just rm -rf.
In Codex, the sandbox goes on the loop line, not in the hope of the config.
